message.content: I'll pass on the list price and put Pacific up for auction so I can keep a cash buffer against the dark-blue rents.
message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to buy Pacific Avenue or start an auction.

I have $486 cash and no monopolies yet. Pacific Avenue costs $300, leaving me with $186. Player 1 owns a dark blue monopoly with houses on Boardwalk and Park Place. Rent there is $600, which I cannot afford without mortgaging. Buying Pacific would leave me short for that rent.

Mortgaging my current properties yields about $370. Adding Pacific Avenue's $150 mortgage would give me roughly $706 total. That covers the $600 Boardwalk rent, so buying Pacific is viable.

I am reconsidering the purchase. The green group is expensive to build, and I have no partners to help me develop it. Other players also hold large cash reserves and several properties.

Player 4 owns Oriental, Connecticut, St. James, Atlantic, and Water Works with $1310 cash. Player 1 has only $64 but controls the lethal dark blue set. I should avoid draining cash on Pacific Avenue since I own none of the three green properties yet.

Auctioning Pacific Avenue could let other players acquire it cheaply. They have enough cash to develop greens later, so I should not spend $300 on a property that is not on my priority list.

Boardwalk with two houses costs $600, which I cannot pay from cash alone. Park Place with one house costs $175, which I can cover. Buying Pacific Avenue would leave me with only $186, making the Boardwalk rent even more unaffordable.

I will start an auction for Pacific Avenue. Declining the purchase triggers an auction where I can bid later for less than $300.

I will only bid on Pacific Avenue if the price drops below $200. If other players raise the bid, they will drain their cash reserves. A lone winner might claim it for a dollar, but that is unlikely. North Carolina and Pennsylvania are still unowned, so completing the green set remains a long-term goal rather than an immediate threat.

I will publicly downplay Pacific Avenue to discourage aggressive bidding. Player 1 has only $64 and cannot afford a high auction price. This should let me acquire the property cheaply if the bid drops below $300.
